headline: GOLD FALTERS AT $4,394 AS 10-YEAR TREASURY YIELD NEARS ONE-YEAR HIGH OF 4.72%
snippet: Gold pulled back to $4,394 Tuesday as rising U.S. Treasury yields competed with safe-haven demand, with the 10-year benchmark hitting 4.72% near a one-year high. Markets still expect the Fed to hold steady in September, limiting the downside.

headline: COPPER SINKS 2.09% TO $6.47 AS CHILE CUTS 2026 OUTPUT FORECAST AND CHINA DEMAND SOFTENS
snippet: Copper dropped sharply Tuesday after Chile's mining authority flagged a 2.6% cut to its 2026 output forecast amid persistent mine setbacks, while demand signals from China weakened. The reversal follows last week's push above $6.70 and leaves LME spreads historically tight despite the pullback.

headline: THREE LITHIUM MINES RESTART: CATL JIANXIAWO CLEARS PERMITS, BALD HILL AND FINNISS BACK ONLINE
snippet: CATL's Jianxiawo mine — one of the world's largest lithium deposits — has cleared security permits and is restoring output following a prolonged suspension. Simultaneously, Mineral Resources is restarting Bald Hill after 18 months on care and maintenance and Core Lithium's Finniss project is also back, easing near-term deficit fears that had pushed lithium to 153,500 CNY/T.

headline: CHINA RELOADS CRITICAL MINERALS ARSENAL — BULL MARKET HAS OFFICIALLY LAUNCHED, INVESTORNEWS DECLARES
snippet: China's renewed deployment of export controls on rare earths and critical minerals is the trigger InvestorNews says confirms the long-anticipated bull market has arrived. Washington is accelerating domestic supply chain buildout in response, with Rio Tinto and BHP summoned to a White House critical minerals meeting.

headline: RARE EARTH PRICES PULL BACK AFTER JULY RALLY — MALAYSIA WEIGHS EASING 2024 EXPORT MORATORIUM
snippet: Rare earth oxide prices retreated in August after a strong July surge, with erbium the sole exception bucking the trend. Malaysia is reassessing whether to lift its 2024 moratorium on raw rare earth exports as investors from the U.S., Australia, France, and India intensify lobbying pressure.

headline: BLUE MOON METALS ACQUIRES 33 U.S. TUNGSTEN AND ANTIMONY PROJECTS FOR $20.5M
snippet: Blue Moon Metals completed the acquisition of 33 tungsten and antimony projects across the western U.S. for US$20.5M ($5M cash plus 2.8M shares at $5.55), significantly expanding its critical minerals footprint as Washington pressures industry to break Chinese dominance in strategic materials.

headline: GOLD MINERS Q2'26: SECOND-BEST QUARTER EVER AS $4,300 GOLD OFFSETS 7%+ COST INFLATION
snippet: Major gold miners just reported their second-best quarterly results on record, with operating margins holding strong at $4,300+ spot gold even as labor, energy, and maintenance costs rose sharply. G Mining typified the sector — raising cost guidance 7% while holding production targets — but the margin story remains compelling.

headline: GDX POISED FOR NEW ALL-TIME HIGHS BY YEAR-END AS SECTOR RE-RATING ACCELERATES
snippet: Technical and fundamental analysis converge on a year-end breakout target for GDX, with gold miners trading at historically cheap valuations despite record bullion prices. The analysis argues earnings leverage to $4,300+ gold is finally flowing through to share prices after a multi-quarter lag.

headline: AZTEC TOMBSTONE: 88.4m AT 1.42 g/t Au AND 14.58 g/t Ag — NORTH EXTENSION STEP-OUT VALIDATES LARGER SYSTEM
snippet: Aztec Minerals' first North Extension step-out at its Tombstone property in southeastern Arizona returned 88.4 metres averaging 1.42 g/t Au and 14.58 g/t Ag (1.69 g/t AuEq) from 10.7 metres depth, confirming mineralization extends significantly beyond the known resource in a historic Arizona gold-silver district.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING Q2 RECORD REVENUE: 23 RIGS RUNNING, $30-40M EXPLORATION BUDGET TRACKING ON PLAN
snippet: Discovery Mining (DSV.TSX) posted record Q2 2026 revenue with strong year-over-year earnings growth, reporting up to 23 exploration drill rigs operating as of August 12. The company is tracking toward its $30–$40M expensed exploration budget for the full year.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $87.75 AS META AND MICROSOFT NUCLEAR DEALS CONFIRM AI DATA CENTER DEMAND SHIFT
snippet: Spot uranium held at $87.75/lb Monday — up 19.55% year-over-year — as Meta and Microsoft signed agreements to secure nuclear capacity for AI data center operations. Kazakhstan lifted H1 2026 production 9% year-on-year, providing some supply offset, while geopolitical tension in power markets continues to underpin prices.

headline: MEXICO AND PERU MINERS OUTPERFORM AS GOLD HOLDS $4,400 AND SILVER STEADIES AT $65
snippet: Latin American precious metals miners — led by Mexican and Peruvian producers — outperformed global peers Tuesday as gold held above $4,400 and silver steadied near $65 after Monday's Comex profit-taking. The region's lower-cost operations are benefiting disproportionately from sustained high metal prices.
